content.title: Cardiac magnetic resonance in patients with suspected myocarditis
content.summary: Guidance on use and interpretation of CMR (T1/T2-weighted sequences and LGE) for suspected myocarditis, including indications, main findings, diagnostic significance, and timing of imaging changes.
indication: Indicated at baseline in all patients with clinical history + ECG, elevated troponin or echocardiographic abnormalities, when significant CAD is excluded or unlikely.
Advised at follow-up in patients with persistent dysfunction on echocardiography, arrhythmias, or ECG abnormalities.
main_findings: At baseline: T1-weighted (inflammation, injury) and T2-weighted (oedema) sequences, extracellular volume and LGE within 2 weeks after symptom onset.
At follow-up: use LGE to evaluate degree of scarring, and T1 and T2 to identify persistent inflammation.
diagnostic_significance: At least one T2-based criterion (global or regional increase of myocardial T2 relaxation time or increased signal intensity in T2-weighted images), with at least one T1-based criterion (increased myocardial T1, extracellular volume, or LGE) in the acute phase.
Only one marker (T2-based or T1-based) may still support a diagnosis of acute myocardial inflammation in an appropriate clinical scenario, but with less specificity in the acute phase.
A negative T1/T2 scan does not exclude an ongoing inflammatory process in the chronic phase.
timing_and_evolution: It takes at least 3 months before CMR signs of oedema (secondary to inflammation in the acute phase/baseline) disappear.
At 6 months, T1 or T2 signs of oedema should have disappeared if inflammation would be completely absent.
Absence of T1 or T2 oedema does not exclude chronic low-grade inflammation.
